ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, point B is in the first quadrant. $BA \perp x$-axis at A, $BC \perp y$-axis at C, $BA = 3$, and $BC = 5$. There is an inverse proportion function graph that exactly passes through point B. Find the expressions of the inverse proportion function that passes through point B and the linear function that passes through points A and C, respectively.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ BA $\perp$ x-axis at A, and BC $\perp$ y-axis at C, with BA $= 3$ and BC $=5$, \\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point B are $(5,3)$, point A $(5,0)$, and point C $(0,3)$.\\
Let the inverse proportional function be $y = \frac{k}{x}$ ($x \neq 0$),\\
$\because$ point B lies on the graph of the inverse proportional function,\\
$\therefore k=3 \times 5 = 15$\\
$\therefore$ the equation of the inverse proportional function is $y = \frac{15}{x}$;\\
Let the linear function be $y = ax + b$,\\
Substituting A$(5, 0)$ and C$(0, 3)$, we get\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
b=3\\
5a+b=0
\end{array}\right.$\\
Solving gives:\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
a=-\frac{3}{5}\\
b=3
\end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore$ the equation of the linear function is $\boxed{y = -\frac{3}{5}x + 3}$.
